questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $4y+12{y}^{′}=0.$ 

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=0,1,2,…?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{′}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+12{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the second sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+12{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the second summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+12{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[4{a}_{n}+12(n+1){a}_{n+1}]{x}^{n} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
4{a}_{n}+12(n+1){a}_{n+1}=0.
$$

Finally, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+1}=-\frac{{a}_{n}}{3(n+1)},\,n=0,1,2,….
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}-4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}3{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}-4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}-4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
3(n+1){a}_{n+1}-4{a}_{n}=0.

questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $3xy-2{y}^{′}=0.$

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=1,2,3,…$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{′}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}-2{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }3{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the second sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }3{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}-{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }2(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Now, in the first series, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n+1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=1}^{\infty }3{a}_{m-1}{x}^{m}-{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }2(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in both summations (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }3{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }2(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Next, we need to get two series starting with the same value of $n.$ So, we take out the term $n=0$ from the right-hand side:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }3{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}-2{a}_{1}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We now combine the series, as follows:

$$
-2{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[3{a}_{n-1}-2(n+1){a}_{n+1}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Finally, by equating coefficients of ${x}^{n},$ we obtain

$$
{a}_{1}=0,\,2(n+1){a}_{n+1}=3{a}_{n-1}.
$$

Solving for ${a}_{n+1}$ gives

$$
{a}_{n+1}=\frac{3{a}_{n-1}}{2(n+1)},\,n=1,2,3,….
$$

Note that every coefficient with an odd index is equal to $0,$ since ${a}_{1}=0.$

questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $3{y}^{″}-2y=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for ${a}_{n}$ can be written as

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{f(n)},\,n=0,1,2…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find ${y}^{″}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
3{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}-2{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-2.$ This gives

$$
3{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+2)(m+1){a}_{m+2}{x}^{m}-2{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
3{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}-2{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[3(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}-2{a}_{n}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
3(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}-2{a}_{n}=0.
$$

Finally then, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{2{a}_{n}}{3(n+1)(n+2)},\,n=0,1,2…
$$

Therefore, $f(n)=\frac{3(n+1)(n+2)}{2}.$

questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $6y+9{y}^{″}=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for ${a}_{n}$ can be written as

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{f(n)},\,n=0,1,2,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}=0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the second sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-2.$ This gives

$$
6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+2)(m+1){a}_{m+2}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the second summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[6{a}_{n}+9(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
6{a}_{n}+9(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}=0.
$$

Finally, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+2}=-\frac{2{a}_{n}}{3(n+1)(n+2)},\,n=0,1,2,…
$$

Therefore, $f(n)=-\frac{3(n+1)(n+2)}{2}.$

Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $3{y}^{″}+y=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for ${a}_{n}$ can be written as

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{f(n)},\,n=0,1,2,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
3{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-2.$ This gives

$$
3{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+2)(m+1){a}_{m+2}{x}^{m}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
3{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[3(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}+{a}_{n}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
3(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}+{a}_{n}=0.
$$

Finally, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+2}=-\frac{{a}_{n}}{3(n+1)(n+2)},\,n=0,1,2,…
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Let $y = \displaystyle{\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^n}$ be a series solution to the equation $y'-3y=0$.
What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients $a_n$, where $n=0,1,2, \ldots$?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $y'(x){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and $y'(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\sum_{n=1}^\infty n a_n x^{n-1}-3\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^n = 0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m = n-1$. This gives

$$
\sum_{m=0}^\infty (m+1) a_{m+1} x^{m} -3 \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^n =0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty (n+1) a_{n+1} x^{n} -3 \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^n =0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0$, we can combine them as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }3{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}-3{a}_{n}{x}^{n}] & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[(n+1){a}_{n+1}-3{a}_{n}]{x}^{n} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
(n+1) a_{n+1}  -3 a_n = 0.
$$

Finally then, the recursion formula is

$$
a_{n+1} =\dfrac{3 a_n }{n+1}, \qquad n= 0,1,2, \ldots
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Let $y =\displaystyle{\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^n}$ be a series solution to the equation $2y''+y=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for $a_n$ can be written as

$$
a_{n+2} = \dfrac{ a_n }{ f(n) }, \qquad n= 0,1,2\ldots
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $y'(x)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find $y''(x)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and $y''(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
2\sum_{n=2}^\infty n (n-1) a_{n} x^{n-2} +\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^{n} = 0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m = n-2.$ This gives

$$
2\sum_{m=0}^\infty (m+2) (m+1) a_{m+2} x^{m} +\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^{n} = 0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
2\sum_{n=0}^\infty (n+2) (n+1) a_{n+2} x^{n} +\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n x^{n} = 0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }2(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[2(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}+{a}_{n}{x}^{n}] & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[2(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}+{a}_{n}]{x}^{n} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
2(n+2)(n+1) a_{n+2}  +a_n = 0.
$$

Finally then, the recursion formula is

$$
a_{n+2} = -\dfrac{ a_n }{ 2(n+1)(n+2)  }, \qquad n= 0,1,2 \ldots
$$

Therefore,

$$
f(n)=-2(n+1)(n+2).
$$
